newsitem.title: CHINA: China should limit domestic grain trade role - paper.
newsitem.headline: China should limit domestic grain trade role - paper.

text.p: China's grain authorities should limit their role in the domestic market as part of a plan to reform the sector, the China Daily said on Monday.

State grain departments should separate their role as buyers and sellers of grain from that of market regulators, the newspaper quoted Zhang Congming, a board member of the China Association of Rural Economy, as saying.
State grain departments had failed to control fluctuations in the grain markets despite huge government subsidies, the newspaper said.
Grain authorities should focus on regulating market activity, such as supervising prices, rather than direct buying and selling, Zhang said.
The newspaper said enterprises should be encouraged to take a greater role in the trading of grain. It did not give details of how this would work.
China buys grain from farmers and subsidises the cost of the grain when it is sold to consumers.
Beijing said earlier this month it would launch an ambitious reform of its agricultural sector, unifying the price the state pays for grain with the market rate, starting next year.
China has forecast a record grain harvest of about 480 million tonnes for 1996, some 15 million tonnes more than last year's bumper crop.
